maps-j-05049.passage:
## The narrowed same-id-twice stop rule

Before this item, `merge-loop`'s stuck-twice stop rule fired on *any*
repeated block reason for the same id, indiscriminately — a
`verify-timeout-post-merge` and an Iron Law block were treated the same
way even though only one of them could ever self-resolve. The rule now
applies only to a reason that genuinely has no playbook: once a playbook
exists for a reason, retrying it is the playbook's own job (each playbook
above defines its own single-retry-then-escalate shape), and the loop's
generic same-id-twice rule stops competing with it. A successful merge
for any id resets both the blocked-id tracking and any in-flight playbook
attempt; the run's accumulated Iron Law list is the one thing a
successful merge never resets, since those still need a person regardless
of what else the loop does afterward.

maps-j-05055.passage:
## D7: lock merge by target ref, not a global concurrency cap

Direction A's own real design decision, once reached: rather than
capping "how many merges may run at once" with one global number, the
lock is keyed by **target ref** (`mergeSlotLockFile(targetRef)`,
`src/runner/main-checkout-lock.mjs` — `encodeURIComponent`-based, so
distinct refs always produce distinct, collision-free lock filenames).
Two merges landing on different target branches can run concurrently
with no shared lock at all; two merges racing the *same* target branch
still serialize, because that's the only pair that can actually collide.
This is the direct answer to cause 1 above: the lock stopped being
"one lock, one repo" and became "one lock per thing that can actually
conflict."

`tsk-xyr` is the item that carried D7 to landed code. Its own scout
evidence pinpointed where the old repo-wide lock actually cost the most:
leaf-to-root merges were already isolated onto a **detached** worktree at
the tip of `fgw/<rootId>` (`bin/fgos.mjs:3145`, via
`withMergeEphemeralWorktree`, landing with `git branch -f` — a comment at
`:3110-3117` even says "never the human's own main checkout"), yet the
very next line, `:3150`, still passed `lockRoot: repoRoot` — claiming the
one shared main-checkout lock for a merge that never touched that
checkout at all. Two leaves under different roots contended for nothing
real. `src/runner/write-queue.mjs`'s own docstring ("a sequential async
write-queue primitive") confirmed it was never a per-root mutex either,
despite an older comment nearby claiming otherwise — overlap was only
ever *detected* after the fact (the CAS guard from `tsk-46a`), never
*prevented*, until this item's target-ref lock closed that gap directly.

## 3. Work Item Data Dictionary

| # | Element | Meaning | Values | Required | Default |
|---|-------|---------|--------|----------|---------|
| 1 | id | Định danh bền của work item, dạng kebab-case chữ thường, mở đầu bằng chữ cái; không trùng. KHÔNG mang nội dung title (title lưu ở field riêng #2) — item gốc sinh tiền tố cố định `tsk-` + hậu tố ngắn chống trùng; item con (sinh qua chia-việc) mang id `<id-của-gốc>-<n>` (n = thứ tự trong lứa con, đệ quy nếu con lại bị chia tiếp) | ví dụ `tsk-e5i0f2` (gốc), `tsk-e5i0f2-1` (con thứ 1) | yes | — |
| 2 | title | Tên việc người đọc hiểu; nhận mọi ký tự unicode | free text | yes | — |
| 3 | kind | Loại việc (trả lời "việc này thuộc loại gì" — câu 2 của sáu câu) | free text | yes | — |
| 4 | status | Trạng thái vòng đời; schema từ chối giá trị ngoài **mười** trạng thái này (phạm trù `validation`) kể cả qua tầng thư viện. Chuỗi chính chạy `todo → doing → awaiting-approval → delivered → retrospective → cleanup → done`, cộng ba nhánh rẽ `blocked`/`awaiting-human`/`wontfix`. Bốn chặng ĐUÔI (`delivered`/`retrospective`/`cleanup`/`done`) là chuỗi dùng chung mọi domain đi y hệt nhau, không domain nào được đặt nhãn lại. **Phân biệt durable status vs effective status:** Trạng thái bền (**durable status**) là view gộp từ nhật ký sự kiện `work.move`. Trạng thái hiệu lực (**effective status**) là trạng thái bền được phủ bởi bản ghi runtime claim đang hoạt động (`.fgos/runtime/claims/<id>.json`), theo công thức `effectiveStatus(item) = activeClaim(item.id) ? 'doing' : durableStatus(item)`. Mọi claim mới KHÔNG BAO GIỜ ghi bền giá trị `doing` vào nhật ký sự kiện (*new claims do not durably write into doing*); `doing` đóng vai trò trạng thái hiệu lực khi claim đang hoạt động, và vẫn giữ giá trị FSM hợp lệ cho dữ liệu di sản hoặc đường phục hồi fallback | `todo` — chưa bắt đầu · `doing` — đang làm · `blocked` — kẹt vì lỗi/runner-park, hai chiều với todo/doing; nhận thêm một cạnh vào từ `awaiting-approval` (per pr-lifecycle / 1359ab5e) khi cổng duyệt gãy — merge conflict hoặc verify đỏ sau merge — mang `reason` bắt buộc, cùng khuôn enforce với `awaiting-approval→todo`; xem spec Runner "Cổng duyệt PR nội bộ"; và một cạnh RA thẳng tới `awaiting-approval` (per fan-out-parallel) khi một lần đồng bộ-lại (catch-up) sạch — cạnh này KHÔNG mang `reason` (mirror khuôn cơ học của `blocked→todo`/`blocked→doing`, khác khuôn bắt-buộc-lý-do của `awaiting-approval→todo`/`awaiting-approval→blocked`) và KHÔNG BAO GIỜ đi qua `doing`; xem spec Runner "Đồng bộ lại một việc đỗ (catch-up)" · `awaiting-human` — đậu chờ người quyết, mang một câu hỏi; runner/frontier KHÔNG BAO GIỜ pick; rời khi người trả lời (một lối vào từ `todo` hoặc `doing`, một lối ra về `todo`); đậu vô thời hạn, không timeout · `awaiting-approval` — goal-check đạt, đề xuất nằm trên nhánh chờ duyệt · `delivered` — code ĐÃ được nhận vào cây chính; đây chính là nghĩa hẹp mà `done` từng mang không chính thức cho phép kiểm "dep đã mở chưa" (RUL12 (frontier dẫn xuất)), nay tách ra thành một chặng riêng có tên · `retrospective` — chặng tổng hợp/học sau-thi-công theo lô, chỗ ở mới của bước Compound-learning sau khi nó thôi làm một stage (xem "Mô hình domain" dưới) · `cleanup` — chặng thu-hồi worktree có hạn TTL; một item đỗ ở đây chỉ đi tiếp khi TTL đã trôi qua và phép kiểm thu-hồi đạt, nếu không thì rẽ `cleanup→blocked` · `done` — TERMINAL, nay chỉ còn ĐÚNG MỘT lối vào `cleanup→done`, không bao giờ ra; hai lối vào cũ `doing→done`/`awaiting-approval→done` KHÔNG còn tồn tại — chúng đã được thay bằng `doing→delivered`/`awaiting-approval→delivered`, và phần đuôi nói trên chạy tiếp từ đó · `wontfix` — TERMINAL thứ hai (per fsm-wontfix-terminal-status), cho item bị đóng CHỦ Ý mà không xây (superseded/duplicate/quyết định hành chính), khác `done` (đã hoàn thành thật); ba lối vào — `blocked→wontfix`/`todo→wontfix`/`doing→wontfix` (mirror hai lối vào của `awaiting-human` cộng thêm `blocked`) — không lối ra; KHÔNG bắt buộc `reason` cơ học (cùng khuôn `todo→blocked`/`doing→blocked`), lý do đóng ghi ở decision log của item; `hasOpenDescendant` (`frontier.mjs`) coi `wontfix` là đã-giải-quyết ngang `done` — một con `wontfix` vĩnh viễn không neo gốc ngoài frontier mãi (khác lỗ hổng cũ của `blocked`) | yes | `todo` |
| 5 | deps | Các id item phải xong trước; mọi id phải tồn tại, cấm tự trỏ; "epic" chỉ là một item thường được deps trỏ vào. **Bất biến phi-chu-trình (per work-graph-intelligence S1):** đồ thị `deps` không bao giờ được phép khép vòng — cửa ghi duy nhất (qua verb `add` và `edit`) chặn MỘI lần ghi (thêm mới hoặc sửa `deps`) mà kết quả sẽ tạo một chu trình (A→B→A hoặc dài hơn), ngay sau bước kiểm tồn tại và TRƯỚC khi sự kiện được ghi; lần ghi bị chặn trả lỗi phạm trù `validation` (mã thoát 4). Chu trình được đo qua đúng một đường kiểm tra dùng chung, không có đường thứ hai. Vì id của một item mới phải trỏ tới các id đã tồn tại, một chu trình nhiều-nút chỉ có thể phát sinh khi SỬA `deps` của item đang có; lần ghi thêm mới chỉ có thể tự-trỏ (đã bị chặn từ trước ở bước kiểm hình dạng). Trước bất biến này, một lần sửa `deps` có thể tạo chu trình A↔B mà lọt qua âm thầm (phép kiểm deps khi đó chỉ xét sự tồn tại của id) — lỗ hổng đó nay đã đóng. **Mở rộng (per work-graph-intelligence S2a / record ADR0012 (đồ thị typed-edge derive trên work item — deps→blocks, parent→parent-child, bảo đảm acyclic hợp nhất)):** bất biến phi-chu-trình nay phủ ĐỒ THỊ CẠNH-ĐỊNH-KIỂU HỢP NHẤT (`blocks` từ `deps` + `parent-child` từ `parent`), không chỉ riêng `deps` — xem quy tắc RUL44 (đồ thị cạnh-định-kiểu hợp nhất — bất biến phi-chu-trình toàn đồ thị) và Data Dictionary #13 | danh sách id | yes (rỗng được) | `[]` |
| 6 | risk | Mức rủi ro của việc (câu 4) | free text | yes | — |
| 7 | refs | Đọc gì trước / chạm contract nào (câu 1 + 3) | danh sách tham chiếu | yes (rỗng được) | — |
| 8 | verify | Proof gì thì xong (câu 5) | free text | yes | — |
| 9 | learn | Link bài học để lại (câu 6 — chỗ cắm vòng học sau này) | text | no | — |
| 10 | size | Độ lớn, công sức của việc ('light' · 'standard' · 'heavy') để ước lượng và chia việc, không bao giờ dẫn tới model (Phase 3 tách từ tier cũ; event cũ có tier được map thành size lúc đọc ở một chỗ duy nhất) | `light` · `standard` · `heavy` | no | `standard` |
| 10b | rigor | Độ nghiêm của việc (cùng thang với step và unit), dẫn tới model qua runner.rigorToTier; discovery phán từ bằng chứng thật | `low` · `standard` · `high` · `critical` | no | vắng mặt (dispatch dùng mặc định `standard`, trừ `risk: heavy` dùng `high`) |
| 11 | mode | Chế độ submit đã dùng khi item được tạo qua `submit` — quy ước NGƯỜI-GỌI-NÀO-NÊN-CHẠY-DISCOVERY-TRƯỚC (agent đang sống hay runner tự hành), KHÔNG phải điều kiện mà code rẽ nhánh (xem RUL17 (mode là quy ước gọi, không phải điều kiện code)) | `sync` (mặc định — người submit tương tác ngay) · `async` (người submit rời đi ngay) | no | `sync` (khi tạo qua `submit`; vắng mặt trên item tạo qua `add`) |
| 12 | workflowStep | Bước của item trong Workflow của domain nó (`domains/<domain>/workflows/*.yaml`) — chiều VĨ MÔ của vòng đời, song song với `status` (chiều vi mô, không đổi). Quyết định loại tác vụ/persona nào xử lý item ở thời điểm hiện tại; `status` vẫn áp dụng như cũ BÊN TRONG mỗi bước. **C1 — distinct execution policy.** Publication operates on direct namespace-qualified refs. It refuses symbolic refs in owned and mirror namespaces, validates the destination, and uses a backend mode that cannot follow a symbolic ref outside the grant even if the ref changes after preflight. A plain textual prefix check is insufficient. On the Git floor measured (2.53.0) a plain `update-ref` on a symbolic `refs/fgos/*` ref wrote through to `refs/heads/victim`, and `--no-deref` kept the victim unchanged but silently replaced the symbolic ref with a direct one while the expected-old check passed against the dereferenced value. Two separate checks therefore apply: (1) containment, the guarantee: every ref mutation runs in no-dereference mode with the expected OID on the actual update, so it never changes a ref outside `refs/fgos/*` even when the ref turns symbolic after preflight (the P-SYM-HOOK re-check confirmed this on 2.53.0: every `refs/heads/*` ref unchanged across the attack window, while the control without `--no-deref` moved the victim); (2) refusal, best effort: the ref is read as a symbolic-or-direct fact at preflight and again at read-back, and a symbolic ref found at either point is refused or reported as `recovery-required` tamper evidence. Detection of a **transient** substitution is not guaranteed: the same re-check turned a direct ref symbolic between preflight and the CAS, the `--no-deref` CAS overwrote it with a direct ref at the candidate, and both reads saw a direct ref, so read-back cannot recover the overwritten symbolic state. A substitution that is still present at read-back is detected. No detection mechanism for the transient case is claimed until a proof names one. An expected-OID match is never evidence that the ref was direct. Object writes and reads do not enable replace-object or alternate-object authority from worker input, and every identity/type/tree/ancestry/publication read runs with replacement objects disabled (`--no-replace-objects` or its environment equivalent): scrubbing `GIT_REPLACE_REF_BASE` does not disable repository-owned `refs/replace/*`, which made `cat-file` return a different commit for the same OID in the floor proof. Worker-supplied alternate-object, replace-ref and shallow authority (`GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES`, `GIT_REPLACE_REF_BASE`, `--reference`-style overrides, config injected through the scrubbed env context of G-001/G-183) is always refused. Repository-owned layout in the trusted common dir (`.git/objects/info/alternates`, shallow, promisor remotes) is a compatibility profile: until E5 establishes which of these configurations `fgos-git` supports, an operation that needs an object unavailable under that layout refuses by name rather than fetching implicitly, and the refusal names the layout feature. Raw Git does not do this by itself: a read of a missing blob in a promisor partial clone spawned a lazy `fetch`, and a missing alternate gave a generic exit 128. So the hardened context sets no-lazy-fetch (`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` on the measured floor) for every non-Remote operation (status, diff, read, checkout, merge, not only readObject); shallow, alternates and promisor layout are detected before invocation; a missing object or incomplete traversal becomes a named layout refusal that keeps the actual Git error. Any fetch or deepen is a Remote operation with its own authorization, never an Inspect repair.

**N7 — ownership and mechanism decided (owner decision Q2).** Execution owns continuous custody from producer start through attempt exit, runner commit, receipt and handoff. Worker exit never releases custody. Git validates it and owns the mutation, not attempt scheduling. Successor producer/reset/sync/remove/commit is refused until current generation handoff is proven. Missing/stale custody fails closed. Read-only workflows require no writable custody.

- **RUL93 (the runner loop's worker and the fan-out batch run as one Unit run each, 2026-10-14; ends the `spawnWorker` purpose door of RUL68 (2 tầng dispatch) and the `R3_PENDING_WORK_CALLERS` entries of RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed) for `loop.mjs`, `work-dispatch.mjs` and `fanout-batch.mjs`).** `spawnWorker` (`src/runner/work-dispatch.mjs`) builds the item's Unit with `workUnitFor` and runs it through `runUnit` in the item's worktree, with `session { headless: true, herdrPresent: false }` (the loop never opens a pane, even when the runner itself runs inside herdr); `fanout-batch.mjs` does the same per candidate after `pick`, then `fgos return` on `pass` (no `--worker-verified-sha`: return judges the Unit run's commit) or `return --to blocked` otherwise, reporting each `fired` entry as `{id, unitRunId, outcome, commit}`. The worker runs confined and never commits; the Unit run commits a passing round inside its `writes` (`['**']` for a step), and the loop reads `commit` (`runner`, `none`, or `self` when HEAD moved without a runner commit) instead of committing itself. A step Unit names its capability as its domain's Workflow units do, `<domain>:<verb>` (`coding:discover`), except the coding executing step, which keeps `code:implement`; `bind()` falls back to the bare verb, and `fgos doctor`'s `workflow-capabilities-configured` also names `code:implement` (`RUNNER_LOOP_CAPABILITY_USES`). The worker config is the repo's `.fgos/config.json` (snapshotted into `unit.json`): `fgos-runner` has no `--config` any more. Outcomes map onto the recovery matrix (`src/runner/recovery.mjs`): a failed runner commit, or an index staged before launch, is `worktree-fail`; a timeout `worker-timeout`; a command that cannot start `worker-spawn-fail`; every candidate at its provider limit `provider-limit` (park); a refusal before any worker started `no-executor` (park, the message names `runner.capabilities["<cap>"].prefer`), so one capability without a runnable pool never halts the runner; a round that ran, did not pass and left uncommitted files `worker-failed` (retry), so goal-check never judges files that are not on the branch; a round that did not pass and left nothing resolves with `commit: none` and goal-check decides on the branch as it stands. A round that stopped over its own partial writes (RUL92 (a writing seat is not run again over its own partial writes after a provider limit)) or whose runner commit failed keeps its worktree: the loop notes `{unitRunId, worktree}` under `.fgos/runtime/runner-resume/<id>.json`, and the item's next attempt (a retry, or a later dispatch once the item is back at `todo`) resumes that same Unit run there, so a failed commit is committed again without spawning the agent; the note is checked against `unit.json` (same Unit id, worktree still checked out on `fgw/<id>`) and dropped once the run no longer needs it. The Unit's rigor comes from the operation, then the item's `rigor`, with `risk: heavy` read as `high` only when no `rigor` is declared; bind's floor raises `low` to `standard`. The item's `refs` and `docsRef` enter the Unit only as safe repo-relative paths (others are dropped with a warning that reaches the loop log), and its `prefer` names the step's executor only when that executor is registered. The executor dispatch event carries `unitRunId`; the item log names the run the moment it exists and where its output is captured (`protected/capture/` while it runs, `stdout.log` once it settles), since a Unit run streams nothing back; a write into the main checkout during the round reaches the loop log as a `stray-write-correlated` warning. A pane run's `stdout.log` holds the settled report's text, so a worker run in a pane must put its `fgos-verdict`/`fgos-discovered` fences in its report; the loop reads the first non-empty of report, `stdout.log` and claim summary, never several. The startup reap keeps a 0-commit `fgw/` branch that a killed round still has checked out, with its uncommitted work, instead of failing on the branch delete. Not done: the loop does not resume a Unit run left `running` by a killed runner (the run id is in the item log; `fgos run --resume <unitRunId>`); a worker detached from a killed runner may outlive it; a commit subject falls back to `producer changes` when the worker wrote no claim.

Bản dàn không bao giờ bị xoá khi nguồn không đọc được (đang ghi dở, `agent.db` không mở được, hoặc không xác định được entry) hay khi bản chép không đọc được vì lý do có thể qua (thiếu `node:sqlite`, `agent.db` không mở được): bản chép được giữ ở `pending/` (giới hạn 5 bản mỗi kho login (mỗi account với một kho, mỗi `stores/<cli>` với kho theo CLI), nhưng chỉ bản dư thừa mới bị bỏ: sau khi áp các bản pending dưới account lock, bản có login trùng hệt một bản pending khác thì bị bỏ khi account vượt giới hạn, bản mới nhất của mỗi nhóm trùng được giữ; bản không chứng minh được là dư thừa hay lỗi thời thì không bao giờ bị bỏ để nhường chỗ, nên account có thể vượt giới hạn và check doctor báo; bản do probe ghi dở được giữ ở `torn/` cho việc khôi phục thủ công, không bao giờ tự áp hay tự bỏ, và doctor báo ở mọi tuổi; `torn/` chỉ áp cho bản scratch của probe, còn scratch do runner đã chết để lại và pane home có store bị cắt vẫn bị xoá khi JSON không đọc được; bản không parse được thì so theo byte của file store và của write-ahead log hoặc rollback journal không rỗng (file không đọc được, trừ khi không tồn tại, không bao giờ bị coi là không có; index `-shm` không tính); home có file store trùng từng byte với nguồn và không bên nào có write-ahead log hay journal không rỗng thì không renew gì nên không được dàn) và báo `staged`/`apply-deferred`; chỉ xoá khi nguồn đọc được và chứng minh bản chép không mới hơn, hoặc bản chép được chứng minh hỏng (JSON hỏng, hay không có entry dùng được). Nếu việc dàn thất bại, private home và marker được giữ lại (việc xoá báo lỗi, một dòng stderr mã cố định) để lần xoá sau, kể cả của reaper, thử lại; mỗi lần thất bại được đếm trong marker (`credentialKept`; hai lần cách nhau dưới 15 phút chỉ tính một, để lỗi tạm thời không dùng hết hạn mức), marker được ghi qua file tạm rồi rename và marker có mặt nhưng đọc không được thì việc xoá dừng lại. Sau 5 lần home bị giữ hẳn: không thử xoá nữa, không bao giờ bị xoá vì quá tuổi. Home bị giữ được kiểm lại dưới account lock khi account đó được gia hạn lần kế tiếp và bởi `fgos doctor --fix` (tập temp root tìm kiếm giống của doctor: root mặc định cộng `tempRoot` của từng backend đã đăng ký, lấy qua hook do phía dispatch truyền xuống; home nằm dưới `privateHomeRoot` riêng của backend không thuộc tập này nên không check, repair, reaper hay lần gia hạn nào thấy, và cũng không bao giờ bị xoá), và chỉ với home thuộc đúng runtime dir của lock đang giữ: chỉ xoá khi nguồn đọc được và chứng minh login trong home không mới hơn, hoặc login đó đã dàn được cạnh nguồn (và được áp); không thì vẫn giữ. Bản đã dàn và thư mục `pending/` được đồng bộ xuống đĩa trước khi home bị xoá. File marker không nhận ra được là marker nào cả (không phải JSON, không phải object, hay không có tên contract) thì mọi việc xoá home đó dừng lại. Unresolved records/pins/snapshots never expire by TTL. Doctor reports pending count, retained bytes, oldest unresolved operation and consumer acknowledgement debt. New preparation may refuse with a named storage-capacity cause; it must **never** recover capacity by deleting unknown evidence. Compaction retains request digest and durable terminal receipt needed to reject same-id reuse; a `superseded` chain (rule 4a) is terminal and compacts the same way, keeping its request digest and its `superseded` outcome with the superseding operation id; consumer ack does not make the id reusable. WAL compaction never authorizes event segment deletion. Clarified 2026-10-19: compacted PublicationCas entries retain expected and next along with the request/binding digests and terminal outcome, so `recover(id)` returns the same full terminal receipt (or terminal error with that receipt) under the original publication authority, without replaying a CAS. The version-2 compact ledger uses lossless base64url encoding of hex hashes to keep the 512-byte per-entry bound, including SHA-256 and maximum-length ids. Compaction remains per call. A scan that encounters a disappearing or partial operation chain re-reads its durable ledger entry: a validated ledger proves it terminal and its bytes are counted in the ledger pass; absence or corruption still fails closed. Admission reports deferred compaction errors on stderr and retains the evidence. WAL scans skip `.durable-file-*.tmp` before counting their bound, including the compacted ledger, using the same temporary-name rule as operation readers; installed malformed entries still fail closed. Publication close consumes holder-lock release and returns `{released, leftoversKilled}`, or `lock-release-stuck` with killed count and pids; dropped handles use the same settle (§5 of Holder-lock).

Trước tsk-in1-4, phạm vi CHỈ áp dụng cho `kind: "cli"` (`kind: "task"` được miễn trừ thẳng theo khai báo — lỗ hổng thật: 1 executor `kind:"task"` không có `agentType`, rơi thẳng về `executor` toàn cục qua đường KHÁC `buildAgentTypeExecutor`, đáng lẽ vẫn cần kiểm nếu `executor` đó không phải Claude, nhưng được bỏ qua nhầm). tách `kind` khỏi vai trò "cờ miễn trừ" — `agy` (`kind:"agent"`) VẪN cần `allowCrossProvider` cho backend `agy` CLI không phải Claude của nó, y hệt trước. Vắng mặt hoặc `false` ở `allowCrossProvider` luôn nghĩa là CHẶN (mặc định hạn chế) — không bao giờ đọc ngược thành "cho phép trừ khi đánh dấu nhạy cảm" (per - tsk-32n, xem `docs/history/capacity-cross-provider-governance/CONTEXT.md`+`plan.md`).

- **RUL65b (Provider Capacity Rotator slice 1 — account selection là runtime capacity, không phải placement/fallback).** Khi một Assignment Run đã qua admission và executor thắng cuộc là `kind:"agent"` out-of-process cho provider có inventory global (slice 1: `openai-codex`), runner acquire đúng một account lease dưới lock global trước launch; `dispatch-plan.json` chỉ ghi requirement, không bao giờ ghi selected account trước admission. Ranking cố định: `openLeases` tăng dần, rồi `lastSelectedAt` tăng dần, rồi `stableHash(seed, accountId)`; sticky assignment chỉ được giữ nếu account vẫn present, healthy, non-quarantined. Lease sống theo Run lifetime và chỉ reclaim khi có proof PID-dead/run-dead, không bao giờ vì elapsed TTL. `kind:"tool"`/MCP executors (ví dụ GitNexus) bypass rotator bằng discriminator hiện hữu, dù cùng provider label.

Selection evidence là Run-owned (`provider-capacity-selection.json`, effective execution contract/evidence) và chỉ được persist dạng redacted: provider, account id/label, lease owner, reason codes/quarantine state, `credentialProvisioned`; không persist credential home path, env values, token, `auth.json` bytes, raw digest/SHA-256. Provisioning của invocation bwrap (cli-spawn và herdr-spawn) dùng selected account `credentialSource` để copy vào private home trước spawn — kind `codex-home` copy `auth.json` vào private `CODEX_HOME`, kind `home-files` (`files`: danh sách đường dẫn tương đối, không `..`) copy đúng các file đó vào private home của agent khác (pi, agy), owner-only, giữ exec bit của helper; inventory vẫn chỉ ở `~/.fgos/config.json`, và pane herdr confine dựa vào nó để khởi động đã đăng nhập (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` §13.1, doctor `confined-pane-accounts`); mất/không đọc/copy lỗi thì fail closed trước spawn với class credential-provisioning/config, không quarantine account, không bind-mount real Codex home, và không còn dùng `FGOS_CODEX_CREDENTIAL_HOMES` hash rotation hay executor-id allowlist làm authority placement.

Fault classifier chỉ đọc high-confidence provider stderr, adapter outcome đã biết (`paused-limit`), hoặc structured agent JSON như `stopReason`; không scan prompt/brief/report/general stdout. Quota/rate-limit quarantine account; auth/login/token quarantine dạng manual-clear; credential provisioning/config/test/confinement/work-product failure không quarantine. Chủ máy đặt quarantine tay bằng `fgos dispatch reconcile provider-capacity quarantine --provider <provider> --account <id> --until <ISO tương lai> --reason "<why>"` (quota-limit tạm thời, `detail.kind: owner`; unknown account hoặc `--until` không ở tương lai bị refuse; ghi vào state thật của máy, không theo `--dir`). Classifier cũng đọc giờ reset tuyệt đối codex in ("try again at 6:02 PM", giờ local, lần kế tiếp). Manual clear duy nhất là `fgos dispatch reconcile provider-capacity clear-quarantine --provider <provider> --account <id> --reason "<why>"` (unknown provider/account bị refuse; non-quarantined account bị refuse trừ khi `--force`). `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` và `fgos doctor` chỉ report; doctor không auto-clear auth quarantine. `readOnlyExecutorRedirects` vẫn giữ nguyên trong slice này; không có `providerFallback`, `providerRuntimes`, `providers.<provider>.models`, six-tier runtime wiring, cross-provider fallback, hay retry loop trong rotator.

Provider failure inside a Unit run goes to another account before another provider (decision 0058). A round that ends `provider-limit` is retried as the same executor and invocation under a fresh `-fb<n>` assignment id while another account of that executor's provider is usable (listed in the inventory, not quarantined) and fewer retries than that provider has accounts were spent on this candidate; the lease then ranks the next account as it always does. Only when no account is left does `nextCandidate` walk the capability pool, skipping provider families whose login failed in this unit and still preferring a family the sibling seats did not use. A process that exits non-zero with a dead-credential wording (`AUTH_FAILURE_PATTERNS`, e.g. pi "No API key found for openrouter.") in its last five stderr lines settles as `provider-limit` with `failure.cause: credential`, so the account is quarantined as `auth-token`. A process that exits the same way with a used-up quota as its last words (`QUOTA_LIMIT_PATTERNS` in `provider-auth-failure.mjs`, line-start anchored after an optional `ERROR:`; measured: codex "ERROR: You’ve hit your usage limit. ... try again at 11:39 PM.", 2026-10-13) settles as `provider-limit` with `failure.cause: quota`, with or without an account lease, so a headless cli-spawn round rotates and walks like a pane round; a leased account is quarantined `quota-limit` until the reset the provider printed (the existing `until`, no separate retry field), and a quota stop does not exclude the provider family. The capacity classifier reads the same wordings from the stderr tail only. Rescheduling a run whose accounts and candidates are all used up is not done here (Workflow runner, separate decision). Each attempt records `fallbackFrom.kind` (`account-rotation` or `next-candidate`).

Fallback (Provider Capacity, tầng 1) từng chọn invocation MẶC ĐỊNH của candidate fallback một cách mù — khi 1 executor mang nhiều invocation khác `confinement` (executor-id-consolidation), phép chọn mù đó có thể lặng lẽ hạ cấp 1 primary có confinement xuống 1 fallback KHÔNG confinement. `selectConfinedInvocationId` (`resolve.mjs`) đóng gap này: kiểm CẤU TRÚC thuần ("candidate có invocation nào khai confinement không"), không bao giờ kiểm ngữ nghĩa policy (việc đó vẫn thuộc Confinement Authority, `confinement/authority.mjs`, không đụng tới) — primary có confinement mà fallback không tìm được invocation nào có confinement thì bị refuse thẳng, không âm thầm dispatch hở. Phạm vi CHỈ áp cho đường fallback provider-capacity; đường redirect read-only (RUL trên/Phase D) là cơ chế khác, không đụng tới ở đây. `opPolicy.fallbackExecutors` giữ nguyên `string[]` — không mở rộng thành `{executor, invocation}` (việc đó phải chạm 8+ file ở tầng khai báo Workflow/Operation, không cần thiết khi bản check cấu trúc trên đã đóng đúng gap thật).

- **RUL74 (lazy-probe unlock: an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call that succeeds).** An account quarantined as `auth-token` has no end time: the owner logs in again by hand and fgOS cannot see it. Instead of waiting for a person to run the clear command, a dispatch that finds **no usable account of the provider** makes one real, cheap call per such account (Codex: `codex exec`; an omp profile, a `home-files` source that lists `agent.db`: `omp -p`; a pi account directory, one that lists `auth.json`: `pi -p`; omp is tested before pi), against the account's own home, not a copy, because the owner uses that home and a renewal belongs there. A call that answers clears the lock (audited as `fgos provider-capacity probe`) and the dispatch goes on; one that does not keeps the lock and records the attempt, and no new call is made for that account within a 30 minute cooldown, however many dispatches ask. Only `auth-token` locks are probed: a quota limit ends by itself and any other manual lock is a person's decision. The call is never made while another account of the provider is usable, runs outside the state lock but inside the account lock of RUL75 (so a renewal made by fgOS cannot overlap it; an account whose lock stays busy past two minutes counts as a failed attempt), stops at the first account that answers, and a failure to probe never blocks the dispatch. A credential layout fgOS cannot name (the agy homes of Gemini) has no call, so that account stays locked for a person. The probe is passed to the dispatch by its callers; a caller that passes none changes nothing.

- **RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store, 2026-10-13).** A herdr pane with a private home carries the login of the account the capacity layer leased (RUL65b), but the folder-trust seed (`seedWorkspaceTrust`, `trustStorePaths` in `src/runner/dispatch/herdr-round.mjs`) derived the trust decision from the store of the account the invocation's static env names (`codex-herdr-fgovn`: `CODEX_HOME=${HOME}/.codex-fgovn`). When the two accounts differ and the static one was never asked about the repo, the seed refused (`untrusted-root`) and Codex stopped at "Trust this folder?" (measured 2026-10-13 14:24, run `unit-run-1791876207053-efe6686b/reviewer/1/runs/01`: the leased `tetcu72` trusts `/home/vantt/projects/forgentX`, `~/.codex-fgovn/config.toml` did not; reproduced read-only with a scratch static home: the main-branch code blocked on herdr rule `trust_directory`, the fixed code settled confined). Now the leased credential source travels with the dispatch (`executeThroughConfinement` adapter option `trustAccountSource` -> herdr-spawn adapter -> the round), and for a round with its own private home the decision is read from that account's store: a `codex-home` source's `config.toml`, a `home-files` source's agy settings. A declared `trustStore.path` still wins; a round without a private home still reads the invocation's home, because that is what its CLI reads. Codex hook trust, seeded from the same root, follows. The "trust vanishing" of 2026-10-07 (another Codex session rewriting an account `config.toml`) is a separate cause this does not remove: it still bites when the leased account's own entry is lost. Not proven: whether Codex 0.160 honours trust given to an ancestor directory (`/home/vantt/projects`); the seed still requires the repo root itself.

- **RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI: one login store per CLI, quota and locks per account, 2026-10-13).** One provider account may be used through several CLIs (Codex, pi, omp), and each CLI keeps its own login store, so an account declared with a single `credentialSource` gave every confined CLI the one store (openai `tetcu72` declared its Codex home, so its confined pi invocations got a Codex login and pi failed on its own directory, RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)). An account in the machine-global inventory now declares exactly one of `credentialSource` (one store, used for every CLI, unchanged; other projects use it) or `credentialSources` (`{ <cli>: <source> }`, the key is the basename of an invocation's `command`: `codex`, `pi`, `omp`, `agy`; each source has the same `kind`/`home`/`files` shape). Every reader takes the store of the CLI actually dispatched: the confinement request (`buildConfinementRequest`) resolves `providerCapacity.credentialSource` from the invocation's command, so private-home provisioning, the write-back marker and the folder-trust seed (RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store)) see that store, and a CLI the leased account has no store for is refused before the worker starts (`credential-provisioning`). The lease does not know the invocation unless it is pinned (`cliOverride.preferInvocation`, as Workflow units and the account probe pin it): a pinned lease only picks an account that has a store for the pinned CLI (`provider-capacity.no-account-for-cli` when none has); an unpinned lease picks among all accounts as before. Refresh-ahead (RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home)) runs before the invocation is settled, so for a per-CLI account it renews the store of each CLI the executor may still launch (the pinned one only, when pinned); the lazy unlock probe (RUL74 (an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call)) calls through the store of the first such CLI. Renewal copies of a per-CLI store wait under `account-locks/<provider>/<account>/stores/<cli>/` (`pending/`, scratch homes, cooldown), never beside another store's copies, and the marker records the store; the account lock stays one per account, and `credential-copies-retained` reads both places. A copy left where the account's current layout does not read (the account directory after the account moved to one store per CLI, `stores/<cli>` after it went back to one store or dropped that CLI, or an account the inventory no longer lists) is never applied, moved to the new layout or dropped: when the machine-global inventory was read, the check fails on it at any age (a torn copy and an over-limit pending directory there included) and names that directory for hand recovery; when the global config cannot be read or is refused by the validator, the check fails instead, names the reason (an error class and the config path, never the parser's own text), lists every retained copy at any age and promises nothing about a dispatch, since a dispatch could not run on that config either. Quota, leases, quarantine and rotation stay per account: no account is split into pseudo-accounts per CLI. The account probe (RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)) leases an account into each confined CLI it has a store for. `confined-pane-accounts` in `fgos doctor` checks each pane against the store of its own CLI. An fgos release from before this rule refuses an inventory that uses `credentialSources` (unknown account key), so the inventory is changed only after the release that reads it is active. The same store directory also holds `torn/` (a login store a probe left half-written, kept for hand recovery and never applied or dropped), and a crash during staging can leave `pending/.tmp-<pid>-<id>`: `credential-copies-retained` reports it once its writer process is gone and it has not changed for ten minutes, and `fgos doctor --fix` removes one only after claiming it by rename (so a writer that is still running loses its own rename and keeps its home) and only when it is empty, has the same files as a copy the store keeps in `pending/` or `torn/` (the shared-memory index aside), or, under the account lock, the source login of the account shows it is no newer or it is malformed; never by age, and any other stays for hand recovery. A staging in a store the account's layout no longer reads is reported once with the stranded copies and is never touched. The doctor check and fix also read the `tempRoot` and `privateHomeRoot` a registered backend declares (absolute, without duplicates) for kept homes; the orphan reaper, the dispatch retries and the root-mode tightening stay on the default temp root, since they delete and re-mode what they find. Nothing retries a kept home under a scan-only root by itself, so doctor treats one as held at once (a failure naming the path) and `--fix` settles it by the same rule as any held home. Not built: per-CLI stores for an unconfined invocation, which keeps naming its store through its own env.

- **RUL91 (a person may pin the provider account of a unit run; the pin is hard and never bypasses the lease, 2026-10-14).** `fgos run --account <id>`, or an `account` key on an `--override` object (one shape; a Unit carries no account), pins a provider account (`src/runner/execution/account-pin.mjs`). `bind()` pins it on each seat its override reaches whose bound executor's provider (normalized as the lease does) lists it in `providers.<provider>.accounts`: `binding.account = { provider, id }`, `provenance.account = { value, source: override:<origin> }`. A seat on another provider (a checker must use another family), an executor without an account list, and a tool or inline binding bind unpinned with `provenance.account.skipped { reason, detail }`; the pin never chooses the executor (pair it with `--provider`); a malformed id is refused (`account-pin-invalid`), and an inherited object key is never an account id. Before the unit run exists the seats are dry-bound as the run would bind them (`simulateUnitBindings` with the run's overrides): a pin no seat takes, or a quarantined account (the message names `until` and the reason code), is refused. A pinned seat is dispatched with the inventory narrowed to its account (`configPinnedToAccount`, as RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI) does), so the lease, quarantine and governance apply unchanged. A provider limit on a pinned seat ends it (`fallbackExhausted.reason: account-pinned`, `retryStopped` on the attempt): no account rotation, no executor failover. `--account` is refused with `--resume`; a resumed run keeps its bindings' account and is refused while that account is quarantined. Left open: the login store per CLI (RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI)) is checked only by the lease at dispatch, after the unit run exists; `capacityProviderOf` derives the provider from the executor entry and can differ from the lease's for an executor that declares no `providerModel` (every configured executor declares one); `fgos workflow start` has no `--account`.

- `src/runner/execution/account-pin.mjs` — ghim account (RUL91 (a person may pin the provider account of a unit run)): `resolveAccountPin` (bind() gọi), `runnerConfigForBinding` (inventory thu hẹp cho dispatch), `assertPinnedAccountsUsable` (quarantine trước unit run/resume), `capacityProviderOf`.

1. The lock description is always `FD_CLOEXEC`. The one moment it is not is inside exactly one spawn that borrows it, through an explicit fd mapping (Node: a `stdio` slot; Rust: `dup2` in `pre_exec`).

The borrower test used by a hook has three conditions, all required: `FGOS_LOCK_FD` names exactly the slot, `fstat(slot)` has the same `dev:ino` as the lock file, and `LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB` on the slot succeeds (a description that already holds the lock succeeds; a sibling that opened the file itself fails). Missing any one, the hook tries the lock once on a description of its own and never claims to be a borrower. The worker base env of a dispatch scrubs `FGOS_LOCK_FD` and `FGOS_MAIN_LOCK_HOLDER_PID`; a leaked variable is useless without the description.

Unix uses the existing `run_borrowed` spawn door and explicit slot-3 mapping, environment annotation, git auto-gc/maintenance disabling, driver preparation and release rule. It introduces no additional containment backend or suspended-start barrier. Predecessor handling stays unchanged: Linux borrows declare no new predecessor record and clean up the borrowed child's process group and descendants; macOS uses the child's process group. Git Publication disables hooks in its own driver before calling this port, as Git spec §10 rule 4a requires.

**One door.** Code reaches the main checkout through `withMainCheckout(scope, purpose, fn)`, which acquires the mutex in the caller's `LockScope` (section 9) and hands `fn` a `mainHandle`. A function that must write under the lock (the `.fgos` checkpoint) takes the handle as a required argument and never acquires by itself. A caller that already holds main (claim) passes its handle down; a merge holds only its slot while it merges and verifies in a temporary worktree, and calls `withMainCheckout` just for the checkpoint, the merge commit and the land. The order in a scope is fixed by rank: merge slot 20, `worktree-admin` 40, main checkout 50 (the state store locks sit at 60 in the registry).

**The merge slot** is a mutex per target ref (rank 20), at `<fgosDir>/locks/merge-slot--<encodeURIComponent(ref)>.lock`; the encoded ref is what v1 already wrote. It serialises merges into one ref and is released after the merge, after main.

**Borrowing replaces `FGOS_MAIN_LOCK_HOLDER_PID`.** The holder runs every git child of a checkpoint or merge through `runBorrowed` (section 3), which gives the locked description to exactly that child in slot 3 with `FGOS_LOCK_FD=main-checkout:3` and prepends `-c gc.auto=0 -c maintenance.auto=false` ([contract](../../../packages/holder-lock/contracts/main-checkout-borrow.v1.json)). The `.githooks/pre-commit` hook, which git runs inside that child, is a borrower only when the three conditions of section 5 hold, checked by `fgos internal lock-fd --protocol 1 --borrowed-check <lock path>`. A borrower skips the activity beacon, because the lock proves who is committing. Anything else is a stranger: the hook probes `main-checkout` once with a description of its own, refuses when it is held, and never waits (git already holds `index.lock`, rank 55). The child cannot release the lock for the holder, cannot pass the description on beyond git's own hooks and cannot start anything in the background; the holder waits for the child before the transaction counts as done. The worker base env of a dispatch drops `FGOS_LOCK_FD`; a leaked variable gives nothing without the description.

The state store takes one transaction at a time per clone through `withStateTx(fgosDir, fn, {resource})` ([`src/state/hot-lock.mjs`](../../../src/state/hot-lock.mjs), contract [`hot-lock.v1.json`](../../../packages/holder-lock/contracts/hot-lock.v1.json)). `resource` is `state` (work events, claims, the state view) or `porting-events` (the porting log); both are registry rows of rank 60, kind `hot-mutex`. The mutex replaces `events.lock`, `runtime/claims.lock` and `porting/events.lock`: claims and events are one critical section, so the worker-slot ceiling is checked in the same transaction as the claim. Code that must reach a hot resource gets the transaction object `tx` (`append`, `writeJson`, `writeText`, `rename`, `readJson`, `unlink`; paths confined to the `.fgos`), which is revoked when the callback returns.

`worktree-admin` is a mutex (rank 40, `<fgosDir>/locks/worktree-admin.lock`) with no v1 predecessor and no fence. It wraps every fgOS call of `git worktree add`, `git worktree remove`, `git worktree move` (relocate) and `git worktree prune`. For remove and relocate, the dirty-check of the worktree, the destroy or move, and the registration change run under one hold of the lock, so no other worktree administration can run between the check and the effect (Git lessons G-042, G-155). It stays one lock: there is no second admin lock, and read-only listing takes none. Rank 40 is below main checkout (50), so no wrapped worktree command runs while main is held: a claim creates its worktree after it has released main; a merge creates its temporary worktree under the merge slot (20), before it takes main.

The supervisor still knows no pane: it asks terminal-control (crate `fgos-terminal-control`, called in process) by the **attempt id as key**, and the controller has already allocated the slot (`allocate(key = attemptId, groupKey)`, [terminal-control spec](../terminal-control/spec.md)). 6. After the receipt the steps run; the last, `release-slot`, decides the pane's fate.

**Orphan branch (the supervisor dies).** The gate watches its connection after `AGENT`. EOF **before** `BRIEF_DELIVERED`: it ends the domain (`orphan` / `abandoned-before-brief`) and the agent never saw a brief. EOF **after**: the agent keeps running; the gate polls the outbox every 50 ms for a `result-<N>.json` that parses as JSON (temporary names and half-written files do not count), waits `terminal.orphanSettleMs` once it sees one, then stops the domain (`orphan-result`, receipt `exited`). With no result it runs to the hard ceiling. Adopt then settles from `gate-exit.json` and the outbox, and its `release-slot` step releases the pane. A gate that starts after its supervisor died finds the socket closed (exit 64) and runs nothing.

**`release-slot`.** `close` only for a clean end: outcome `exited`, an outbox result, no `reason` and every earlier step done. Every other end (blocked, timeout, cancelled, carrier lost, a step that failed) **retains** the pane, by default for 24 hours (`terminal.retainFailedPaneMs`, which travels in the envelope; `null` keeps it until a person closes it), so its screen stays readable. The step closes only the pane of its own key, never a tab. An answer of `unknown` from terminal-control gives no receipt (the step is retried by adopt); `unsupported` fails the step. A step that asked for a retry leaves the slot undecided.

- A slot that was `released` as `retain` refuses a later `close` by key (it closes when `until` passes). A caller that keeps a pane for a person and still wants anyone to be able to close it by key (the account probe, the reaper) leaves the slot allocated instead of retaining it; only an explicit retention window uses `retain`.

The only thing Terminal Control writes is one **allocation record**, published once when the slot is allocated. Its shape and the two markers (`launched`, `released`, plus `launch-requested` written before the driver is asked to run anything) are in [allocation-record.v1.json](../../../packages/terminal-control/contracts/allocation-record.v1.json). It lives under the shared state root, per driver and per server incarnation, one file per key.

Everything else is read live: whether the pane still exists, which process runs in it, which panes the tab has. A hint file that maps a group to a tab exists only to find it quickly; it is always checked against the live state before use and dropped when wrong. ## The two options, and what decides between them

When `decompose` was renamed to `planning` (the verb `fgos decompose` →
`fgos plan` and the launcher `/fgOS:decompose` → `/fgOS:plan` followed),
**four** items were open on the old stage name: one `blocked`, one
`awaiting-human`, one `doing`, one more `doing`.

Two of those four were waiting on a person. That is what settled it:
draining first would have traded a technical blocker the renaming session
could clear itself for a human blocker it could not — and this rename was
blocking an entire tree of downstream work. Trading a blocker you control
for one you don't is a loss.

So `decompose` stayed as a **legacy, drain-only alias**:

- still present in the domain's `stages` array,
- still holding its `skillMap` entry,
- still keeping its outgoing edge,
- but carrying **no `stepMap` entry**.

Items already standing there keep resolving to a skill and can finish. No
*new* item can ever land there, because landing requires a `stepMap` entry.
The follow-up is to delete the alias once the count reaches zero.

## Output shape

```json
{
  "execution": {
    "occupied": 11,
    "items": [
      {"id": "tsk-u8w", "sessionId": "6ea94464-...", "claimRole": "session"},
      "..."
    ],
    "ceiling": null,
    "free": null,
    "hasRoom": true,
    "reason": "no-ceiling-configured"
  },
  "admin": {
    "reserved": 4
  }
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `execution.occupied` | Count of work items currently at `doing` — one running item = one slot (D1/D7 in the design doc: a slot is the occupied seat of exactly one rootTask). |
| `execution.items` | One row per running item — diagnostic detail for a human, not paginated; grows with the number of items at `doing`. |
| `execution.ceiling` | The configured `workerSlots.ceiling` value, or `null` when unconfigured. |
| `execution.free` | `ceiling - occupied`, or `null` when there's no ceiling to subtract from. |
| `execution.hasRoom` | `true`/`false` — the actual pre-check answer a launcher acts on. |
| `execution.reason` | Why `hasRoom` reads the way it does, e.g. `"no-ceiling-configured"`. |
| `admin.reserved` | The admin lane's fixed reservation (4 today) — never counted against `execution`, per the design doc's D4/D9 lane split. |

maps-j-05083.passage:
## Steps

1. **Run the read-only verb:**

   ```
   fgos schedule --json
   ```

   Returns:

   ```json
   {
     "waves": [["tsk-a", "tsk-b"], ["tsk-c"]],
     "cycles": [["tsk-x", "tsk-y"]]
   }
   ```

2. **Read `waves`.** Each inner array is one wave — every id in it can be
   dispatched together right now with no footprint conflict between any
   pair in that same wave. Only the current `frontier` (ready-to-pick)
   items are considered; anything not ready doesn't appear at all.

   The algorithm: for each item still unscheduled, add it to the current
   wave unless its declared `footprint` overlaps
   (`footprintOverlapAmong`) with something already placed in that same
   wave; whatever doesn't fit gets deferred to the next wave. An item with
   no declared footprint never conflicts with anything, so it's always
   eligible for the earliest wave it can reach.

3. **Read `cycles`.** This is a separate check — real dependency cycles in
   the work graph's `deps` edges, found via Tarjan's strongly-connected-
   components algorithm over every item regardless of status (not just
   frontier candidates). A self-dependency (an item depending on itself)
   counts as a one-element cycle. A non-empty `cycles` array means the
   dependency graph itself is broken, independent of anything about
   footprints or waves — worth fixing before trusting `waves` at all,
   since `frontier`'s own readiness computation assumes an acyclic graph.
